Where Everybody, Every moment and Every idea counts!
Welcome to our new website!
Stephen Freeman Primary School is a 2 form entry school on the edge of Great Western Park, in Didcot. We passionately believe that ‘everybody; every moment and every idea counts’ and are committed to ensuring that we provide the highest quality education for the children of our local community.
We are firm believers in developing the whole child, and we dedicate a lot of time and resources to our nurture provision. We pride ourselves on the strong links we have with other professional agencies.
The curriculum is exciting and engaging which encourages our children to develop our 8 learning skills. We want our children to develop a sense of responsibility, to be self-motivated, purposeful, creative and reflective in their approach to learning. We encourage the children to communicate effectively and reflect on their experiences while enabling them to overcome barriers with resilience and a willingness to take learning risks.
Upcoming Events/Dates
There are currently no upcoming events.
Newsletters
There are currently no newsletters.
Our Vision
“At Stephen Freeman School, we nurture and empower everyone to aspire beyond their expectations, by cultivating curiosity, celebrating individuality and creating life-long learners to contribute positively to the wider community.”
If you require hard copies of any information published on our website, we can provide this free of charge. Please contact our School Office with any requests.

Late or Absence Procedure
Attendance
Parents are responsible for ensuring that their children attend school regularly and on time. This is a legal requirement.
Good attendance enables pupils to make good, consistent progress in their schoolwork.
EVERY SCHOOL DAY COUNTS - Days off school add up to lost learning
Children must attend school unless it is absolutely unavoidable. If your child will be absent from school, please contact the school office on 01235814718 option 1 before the start of the school day. There is an answer service for you to leave a message.
If we do not receive notification we will contact you to confirm the absence. A written letter must be sent to school on the child’s return. Parents should be aware that absence is authorised at the discretion of the Headteacher and that an absence note, in itself, does not authorise an absence.
Absence may be authorised for the following reasons:
If an absence does not fit into any of the above categories it will be registered as unauthorised.

pageCache.pageTitle: Stephen Freeman Primary School - Special Education Needs
pageCache.text:
Special Education Needs
Stephen Freeman School is committed to inclusion. Our school aims to provide an appropriate and high quality education for all children in our care. We believe that all children are entitled to a broad and balanced academic and social curriculum. This will be readily accessible to them and they will be fully included in all aspects of school life.
We believe that inclusion is essential in ensuring the equality of opportunity for all learners whatever their age, gender, sexual orientation, disability, attainment and background. This demonstrates our commitment to valuing the diversity of the school community.
It is accepted that many pupils will experience some form of difficulty at some time in their education. At Stephen Freeman Primary School we aim to match the pupils’ needs, whether they are complex and recognised by an Education and Health Care Plan or of a more specific but temporary nature, with appropriate support. Help may be provided in a variety of ways, ranging from high quality whole class teaching, intensive small group work or one to one support.
Pupils requiring support which is additional to or different from that which is normally provided, have their needs recorded and their progress monitored through a Pupil Profile.
The school works closely with the Local Authority and other agencies to ensure that the needs of all our pupils are met.
Special Educational Needs Coordinator
Email: SENCO2594@stephen-freeman.oxon.sch.uk
Governor responsible for Special Educational Needs
Email: chairofgovernors@stephen-freeman.oxon.sch.uk
Choosing a new school for your child is one of the most important decisions you have to make as a parent. We welcome visits to the school to enable your decision making process. Please contact the school office on 01235 814718 to make an appointment. The Local Authority oversee all admission arrangements including those for children with Special Education Needs and Disabilities (SEND). We ask parents to discuss the child’s needs with the school prior to starting so that appropriate interventions and support can be planned and implemented. Advice from the Local Authority or other agencies may be requested to ensure that the school can meet any needs appropriately.

pageCache.pageTitle: Stephen Freeman Primary School - Reading for Pleasure
pageCache.text:
Reading for Pleasure
At Ridgeway Education Trust, we are passionate about encouraging a love of reading in pupils by ensuring access to a wide range of books as well as cultivating book-related experiences to entertain and inspire them. The rationale for this is the plethora of research that shows far-reaching benefits of Reading for Pleasure, including:
Our Reading for Pleasure lead for the Ridgeway Education Trust is Leoni Barnes and the strategy for encouraging our pupils to develop and maintain a love of reading includes author visits, mentoring from older students and participation in local and national book awards. You can read more about this in The Reading Round-Up, the Ridgeway Education Trust’s Reading for Pleasure newsletter.
You might find the following links helpful in helping to develop your children as readers:
Tips and advice from Book Trust
Book recommendations from Book Trust
Advice for encouraging teens to read
Primary Patron of Reading
We are very excited to announce that the award winning author Jo Cotterill will be the Patron of Reading for our RET primary schools for this academic year (2024-25).
As part of this, Jo will be providing books and activities for our pupils each term, based around a total of three Focus Days over the course of the year. Through these, pupils will learn about empathy, positive mental health and healthy communication.
Jo will also be visiting one of our primary schools on each of the Focus Days and working directly with pupils there.

Safeguarding
Safeguarding at Stephen Freeman Primary School
In this school, Safeguarding and Child protection is a shared responsibility, and we all have a legal duty to ensure the welfare of children. If you have any concerns that a child has been harmed, is at risk of harm, or you receive a disclosure, please contact the main school office as soon as possible and ask to speak to a member of staff with responsibility for safeguarding.
As a school, we follow Keeping Children Safe in Education (KCSiE) and have our own school Child Protection Policy. Please read through these documents which are on display in the reception area and discuss any concerns with a DSL (listed below).
The use of mobile phones and cameras by visitors is strictly prohibited on the premises.
Mrs Jess Lewis, Headteacher & Designated Safeguarding Lead
Miss Sue Shaw, Child and Family Practitioner & Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead
Mrs Deborah Wilson, Child and Family Support Practitioner & Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead
Mr Matt Bews, Deputy Headteacher & Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead
If you have any concerns about the safety of a child, please contact the staff named above via the school office. If you have any concerns outside of school hours regarding the welfare of a child, please call Oxfordshire County Council's Multi-Agency Safeguarding Hub (MASH) on 0345 050 7666. If you have an urgent concern for a child call 999 or 101.
As part of our role to safeguard pupils, please be aware that, like all schools, we have a duty to share information with other agencies where there are any concerns about the safety or well-being of a child.
All school policies relating to the safeguarding of pupils are available for further reference on the website Policies page. Paper copies can be requested from the school office.

pageCache.pageTitle: Stephen Freeman Primary School - Breakfast & After School Club
pageCache.text:
Breakfast & After School Club
Breakfast Club
Breakfast Club runs from Monday to Friday 8.00am to 8.45am. It is a great help to parents who start work early as it provides a safe place for their children to be looked after before the start of the school day.
Children arriving before 8.15 a.m. will be welcomed into school and will be given a choice of a healthy breakfast including bagels, cereal, fruit and yogurts. Craft and other activities are on offer every day. Please note if your child arrives after 8:15 a.m. they will not be able to have breakfast as there is insufficient time before school starts.
Breakfast club costs £5.25 per session, which covers the cost of supervision as well as breakfast food.
For further information or to book a place please use the following email address: office@stephen-freeman.school
We are unable to refund the cost of pre-booked sessions.
After School Club
After School Club runs from 3.15 p.m. to 5.45 p.m. We provide a variety of activities to engage the children and we focus on developing social skills and promoting positive interactions whilst they are with us. The children will be offered a light meal during their session.
The club costs £12.50 per day which covers food and staffing costs.
For further information or bookings please email the school office on: office@stephen-freeman.school
We are unable to refund the cost of pre-booked sessions.
